```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
# The examples use malariasimulation and postie, both in Suggests. Chunks are
# evaluated only when both are installed, so package checks do not need them.
can_run <- requireNamespace("malariasimulation", quietly = TRUE) &&
           requireNamespace("postie", quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = can_run)
```

`fleet` is not yet validated for real use; see the
[status note](https://pwinskill.github.io/fleet/#not-ready-for-real-use).

This article runs the model on a `malariasimulation` parameter list, reads the
output with `postie`, and adds interventions, custom demography, seasonality,
*P. vivax* and the discretisation settings. It assumes familiarity with
`malariasimulation`.

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("pwinskill/fleet")
```

```{r load}
library(fleet)
```

`malariasimulation` builds the parameter lists and `postie` post-processes the
output. Both are in Suggests and are installed separately (see the
[README](https://pwinskill.github.io/fleet/#installation)).

## Running the model

Build a parameter list and set the target EIR, in infectious bites per adult
per year, with `set_equilibrium()`, as for the IBM; the run is seeded at the
corresponding equilibrium. The output age bands are also set on the list: here
clinical and severe incidence in under-5s and at all ages, beside the default
2-10 prevalence band.

```{r basic}
p <- malariasimulation::get_parameters(list(
  human_population = 1000,
  clinical_incidence_rendering_min_ages = c(0, 0),
  clinical_incidence_rendering_max_ages = c(5, 100) * 365 - 1,
  severe_incidence_rendering_min_ages = c(0, 0),
  severe_incidence_rendering_max_ages = c(5, 100) * 365 - 1))

# 15 years at a daily step, seeded at the equilibrium for EIR = 20
out <- run_simulation_ode(timesteps = 15 * 365, parameters = malariasimulation::set_equilibrium(p, init_EIR = 20))

out[1:3, c("timestep", "n_age_730_3650", "n_detect_lm_730_3650",
           "n_inc_clinical_0_1824", "EIR")]
```

The result is `malariasimulation`'s daily table: the columns the IBM would
return for this parameter list, with the same names and meanings. Column tags
give the age band in days, both ends included, so `730_3650` is 2-10 years and
`0_1824` is under 5. `n_*` columns are counts: `n_detect_lm_*` is the number
LM-positive and `n_inc_clinical_*` the day's new clinical cases in the band.
`EIR` is per adult per year. Because the model is a mean field, rates do not
depend on `human_population`, which only scales the counts.

With no interventions the run settles rather than holding exactly still:

```{r flat}
pfpr <- out$n_detect_lm_730_3650 / out$n_age_730_3650   # LM prevalence, 2-10y
range(out$EIR)   # ~20 throughout
range(pfpr)      # a ~0.4% relaxation over the first years
```

Row 1 is day 1, whose state is the seed. LM prevalence in 2-10 year olds falls
from the seed by 0.35% to a low a little over a year in, and is flat to within
0.008% over the last five years. EIR stays within 0.4% of its target.
Incidence moves further from the seed than prevalence does: a few per cent over
the first years at this EIR, and more at higher ones.

This relaxation is expected. The
[malariaEquilibrium](https://github.com/mrc-ide/malariaEquilibrium) seed solves
the model's continuous-time form, so it approximates `fleet`'s fixed point on
the daily clock rather than being that fixed point. `malariasimulation` is
seeded from the same solution and drifts from it too; `vignette("model")` lists
the differences. Burn in before calibrating, and read a settled window rather
than the first days.

## Output

The table goes into [postie](https://github.com/mrc-ide/postie) with the same
calls as an IBM run:

```{r epi}
# prevalence: one <diagnostic>_prevalence_<lo>_<hi> column per age band (years)
prevalence <- postie::get_prevalence(out, diagnostic = "lm")
utils::tail(prevalence["lm_prevalence_2_10"], 3)

# rates: clinical / severe incidence, mortality and DALYs by age band
rates <- postie::get_rates(out)
utils::head(rates[, c("time", "age_lower", "age_upper",
                      "clinical", "severe", "dalys")])
```

Use `diagnostic = "pcr"` for PCR prevalence, and `postie`'s other arguments
(`scaler`, `treatment_scaler`, `life_expectancy` and so on) as for an IBM run.

### Age bands

Bands come from the `malariasimulation` rendering fields on the parameter list,
and each output family is reported over its own fields only:
`prevalence_rendering_*` for detection; `clinical_incidence_rendering_*`,
`severe_incidence_rendering_*` and `incidence_rendering_*` for the three
incidence families; and `age_group_rendering_*` for population alone. A band
need not align with the model's age groups:

```{r bands}
p_bands <- p
p_bands$prevalence_rendering_min_ages <- c(0,  2, 10) * 365
p_bands$prevalence_rendering_max_ages <- c(2, 10, 100) * 365 - 1
p_bands$clinical_incidence_rendering_min_ages <- c(0, 2) * 365
p_bands$clinical_incidence_rendering_max_ages <- c(2, 10) * 365 - 1

out_bands <- run_simulation_ode(10 * 365, malariasimulation::set_equilibrium(p_bands, init_EIR = 20))
grep("^n_detect_lm_|^n_inc_clinical_", names(out_bands), value = TRUE)
```

## Interventions

Interventions are set with the usual `malariasimulation::set_*()` functions and
read from the parameter list; `run_simulation_ode()` has no extra arguments for
them. As in the IBM, settings read on the day (treatment coverage, the drug
mix, resistance, death rates) change on their own timestep, and deployments
(nets, spraying, vaccination, chemoprevention) act from the day after theirs.
`vignette("parameters")` covers every argument.

### Bed nets

```{r nets}
p_nets <- malariasimulation::set_bednets(
  malariasimulation::get_parameters(list(human_population = 1000)),
  timesteps = 5 * 365, coverages = 0.8, retention = 5 * 365,
  dn0 = matrix(0.387, 1, 1), rn = matrix(0.563, 1, 1),
  rnm = matrix(0.24, 1, 1), gamman = 2.64 * 365)

nets <- run_simulation_ode(12 * 365, malariasimulation::set_equilibrium(p_nets, init_EIR = 20))
pfpr_nets <- nets$n_detect_lm_730_3650 / nets$n_age_730_3650
c(baseline = pfpr_nets[1], trough = min(pfpr_nets))
```

Prevalence falls after deployment and then relaxes as the nets decay.
Exponential (log-uniform) and logistic net retention are both supported. Net
usage is the mixture over all past distributions, so repeated distributions
accumulate.

### Seasonal malaria chemoprevention

Chemoprevention and clinical treatment need a drug registered first with
`set_drugs()`. Here, four monthly SMC rounds in children aged 3 months to
5 years:

```{r smc}
p_smc <- malariasimulation::set_drugs(
  malariasimulation::get_parameters(list(human_population = 1000)),
  list(malariasimulation::SP_AQ_params))
p_smc <- malariasimulation::set_smc(
  p_smc, drug = 1, timesteps = c(365, 395, 425, 455), coverages = rep(0.9, 4),
  min_ages = rep(round(0.25 * 365), 4), max_ages = rep(round(5 * 365), 4))
p_smc$prevalence_rendering_min_ages <- round(0.25 * 365)
p_smc$prevalence_rendering_max_ages <- round(5 * 365)

smc <- run_simulation_ode(3 * 365, malariasimulation::set_equilibrium(p_smc, init_EIR = 20))
pfpr_smc <- smc$n_detect_lm_91_1825 / smc$n_age_91_1825   # the 0.25-5y target band
c(baseline = pfpr_smc[1], trough = min(pfpr_smc))
```

SMC, MDA and PMC rounds are applied between days, as in the IBM. A fraction of
the target band equal to coverage times drug efficacy is treated. The clinical
and LM-detectable asymptomatic among them pass through the treated state first,
still detectable and infectious for a few days, and everyone treated is then
protected by a prophylaxis chain matched to the drug's Weibull protection
curve.

### Pre-erythrocytic vaccination

RTS,S through the EPI schedule, with a booster:

```{r pev}
p_pev <- malariasimulation::set_pev_epi(
  malariasimulation::get_parameters(list(human_population = 1000)),
  profile = malariasimulation::rtss_profile,
  timesteps = 1, coverages = 0.9, min_wait = 0, age = round(6 * 30),
  booster_spacing = round(12 * 30), booster_coverage = matrix(0.8, 1, 1),
  booster_profile = list(malariasimulation::rtss_booster_profile))

pev <- run_simulation_ode(12 * 365, malariasimulation::set_equilibrium(p_pev, init_EIR = 20))
pfpr_pev <- pev$n_detect_lm_730_3650 / pev$n_age_730_3650
c(baseline = pfpr_pev[1], year12 = pfpr_pev[nrow(pev)])
```

PEV scales the infection hazard by an age- and time-dependent factor. Efficacy
is averaged over the per-individual antibody distribution the IBM samples (a
4-D Gauss-Hermite rule over `cs`, `rho`, `ds` and `dl`) rather than evaluated
at the profile median. Primary and booster doses, EPI and mass campaigns, and
time-varying EPI coverage are modelled, and a campaign's protection ages with
the cohort it vaccinated. Transmission-blocking vaccines are set with
`set_tbv()`.

## Demography

`set_demography()` sets age-specific mortality, which also reshapes the
equilibrium age structure the run is seeded at:

```{r demog}
dr <- c(0.048, 0.007, 0.003, 0.004, 0.008, 0.020, 0.050, 0.120) / 365
ag <- round(c(1, 5, 10, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100) * 365)

p_dem <- malariasimulation::set_demography(
  malariasimulation::get_parameters(list(human_population = 1000)),
  agegroups = ag, timesteps = 0, deathrates = matrix(dr, nrow = 1))
p_dem$prevalence_rendering_min_ages <- c(0, 0)
p_dem$prevalence_rendering_max_ages <- c(5, 100) * 365

dem <- run_simulation_ode(8 * 365, malariasimulation::set_equilibrium(p_dem, init_EIR = 20))
under5_fraction <- dem$n_age_0_1825[nrow(dem)] / dem$n_age_0_36500[nrow(dem)]
under5_fraction     # ~0.09 here, vs ~0.21 under the default constant hazard
```

Custom demography is time-varying: `mu_age(t)` is interpolated over
`deathrate_timesteps`, so a demographic transition is modelled rather than
frozen. The `t = 0` row also sets the seeded age structure. Match
`default_age_lower(max_age =)` to the top of `deathrate_agegroups`; a warning
is given if the model's age grid runs past it.

## Seasonality

Seasonality is set with the Fourier rainfall parameters. A seasonal run
oscillates around a limit cycle rather than settling to a fixed point. It is
seeded at the annual-mean equilibrium, so the first ~10 years are a transient
onto the cycle, and the annual-mean EIR on the cycle is about 7% below the
aseasonal `init_EIR` target, through nonlinear averaging. Read a burned-in year
for calibration or comparison:

```{r seasonal}
p_seas <- malariasimulation::get_parameters(list(
  human_population = 1000, model_seasonality = TRUE,
  g0 = 0.285, g = c(-0.33, -0.13, 0.052), h = c(-0.35, 0.020, 0.10)))

seas <- run_simulation_ode(20 * 365, malariasimulation::set_equilibrium(p_seas, init_EIR = 20))
final_year <- seas[(nrow(seas) - 365 + 1):nrow(seas), ]
range(final_year$EIR)   # seasonal swing in the settled cycle
mean(final_year$EIR)    # about 7% below the aseasonal target of 20
```

## *P. vivax*

A list from `get_parameters(parasite = "vivax")` runs the *P. vivax* model:
hypnozoite batches and relapse, radical cure with liver-stage protection, and
no severe disease. The output is the IBM's vivax table, which adds relapses and
hypnozoite carriage to the usual columns:

```{r vivax}
pv <- malariasimulation::get_parameters(list(
  human_population = 1000,
  clinical_incidence_rendering_min_ages = 0,
  clinical_incidence_rendering_max_ages = 100 * 365 - 1),
  parasite = "vivax")
pv <- malariasimulation::set_drugs(pv, list(malariasimulation::CQ_PQ_params_vivax))
pv <- malariasimulation::set_clinical_treatment(pv, drug = 1, timesteps = 1, coverages = 0.4)

out_pv <- run_simulation_ode(5 * 365, malariasimulation::set_equilibrium(pv, init_EIR = 3))
tail(out_pv[, c("timestep", "n_inc_clinical_0_36499", "n_relapses",
                "n_with_hypnozoites", "iaa_mean")], 3)
```

Radical cure starts on day 1 here, from a seed without it, so these rows are
still settling towards the treated state; burn in before comparing levels
(`vignette("using")`). MDA, SMC and PMC are refused under *P. vivax*, because
`malariasimulation` itself fails on them.

## Discretisation settings

Numerical settings are the fourth argument of `run_simulation_ode()`, `tuning`:
an `ode_tuning()` object, or a named list of the fields to change. They are the
age grid, the stage counts of the prophylaxis chains, the mosquito sub-steps
per day and, for *P. vivax*, whether hypnozoite batch counts share levels.
Model parameters, the target EIR included, stay on the parameter list, and
every default is the validated choice.

The age grid is the setting most worth changing. The default of 118 groups is
the smallest on which every falciparum claim in `fleetcheck` passes. A grid
under half as fine runs over twice as fast, and is adequate where a result does
not rest on the level of severe incidence or on young children at high
transmission:

```{r tuning}
seas_coarse <- run_simulation_ode(
  20 * 365, malariasimulation::set_equilibrium(p_seas, init_EIR = 20),
  tuning = list(age_lower = default_age_lower(n_group = 53)))

c(default = mean(final_year$EIR),
  coarse  = mean(seas_coarse$EIR[(nrow(seas_coarse) - 365 + 1):nrow(seas_coarse)]))
```

`?ode_tuning` documents every field.

Before relying on a result, read `vignette("using")` for where the mean field
departs from the IBM and what to do about it, and check the relevant claims in
[fleetcheck](https://pwinskill.github.io/fleetcheck/).
